name: Other cohort repos: Kamenqq/air-raid-alerts-forecast, gklymenko/ukraine-air-raid-alerts-time-series, mykhailoisupov/kyiv-air-alert-forecast (+ mykhailoisupov/air-raid-alert-forecast, national), yeliena-bochagova/Time-Series-Analysis-of-air-raid-alerts-in-Ukraine, endrusmah/air-raid-alert-analysis, MaksimPrykhodko/Ukraine-air-raid-prediction
type: repo (7 student / cohort peer repositories from the same KSE Agentic AI School task; mykhailoisupov also has an empty air-raid-alert-forecast-v2 with one commit and only a .gitignore)

Last pushes (UTC): Kamenqq 2026-10-12 18:06 (39 commits); gklymenko 2026-06-21 (8 commits, an earlier cohort/stage); mykhailoisupov kyiv 2026-10-12 21:59 (18 commits) and national 2026-10-12 17:10 (14 commits); yeliena-bochagova 2026-10-12 20:25 (10 commits); endrusmah 2026-10-11 19:20 (5 commits); MaksimPrykhodko 2026-06-24 (3 commits). authors: Kamenqq (single author); Galyna Klymenko (gklymenko, per commit metadata; not the dataset maintainer Vadym Klymenko); Mykhailo Isupov (mykhailoisupov); Yeliena Bochagova; endrusmah (license reads 'Ukraine Alerts As-of project contributors'); Maksim Prykhodko. All built with AI coding agents (Claude Code / Codex), as their READMEs say.
popularity: 0 GitHub stars on every repo except MaksimPrykhodko/Ukraine-air-raid-prediction (1 star), checked 2026-10-17. Licenses: MIT (endrusmah, MaksimPrykhodko); none for the others.
peer_review_status: student repos; all results self-reported; nothing peer reviewed
target_type: A mix, and the mix is the lesson. COUNT targets: Kamenqq (alert starts per oblast per Kyiv day, 1-7 days ahead) and endrusmah (Kyiv City starts per UTC day). gklymenko uses a continuous ACTIVITY target (alert minutes per day, Kyiv City). STATE targets: mykhailoisupov national ('alert active for at least one minute in hour t+h', 24 regions) and Kamenqq's hourly 'chance an alert is active at some moment in each hour'. ONSET targets: mykhailoisupov/kyiv-air-alert-forecast (new alert within 1/3/6 h, quiet city only; the closest match to ours), yeliena-bochagova (at least one new start in the region on day D+1) and MaksimPrykhodko (an alert start in the next hour, Kyiv City, but without masking). The national mykhailoisupov repo measured state inflation directly on one model: Brier skill vs climatology at 1 h is 0.267 on all rows but only 0.065 on rows with no alert at forecast time, and within-region AUC is 0.758 vs 0.620.
target_definition: Kamenqq: count of merged alert episodes starting per oblast per Kyiv calendar day D+k, k=1..7, forecast made at 00:00 Kyiv; hourly 'active at some moment in hour' probabilities. gklymenko: total alert minutes per day for Kyiv City, h=1 day, 80% intervals. mykhailoisupov kyiv: at the top of each hour with no alert active in Kyiv, y=1 if a new alert starts within H in {1,3,6} h. mykhailoisupov national: y=1 if the hour t+h has at least one minute of alert, h in {1,3,6,12,24}. yeliena-bochagova: y=1 if at least one alert STARTS in the region on Kyiv day D+1, info cutoff = end of day D. endrusmah: Kyiv City alert-start count on UTC day D, issued D-1 at 12:00 UTC. MaksimPrykhodko: has_alert(hour)=1 if any Kyiv City alert started in that Kyiv-local hour bin; predicted from lagged hours (H=1).
spatial_unit: Oblast (24 units): Kamenqq, mykhailoisupov national, yeliena-bochagova. Kyiv City only: gklymenko (computed for 25 oblasts but focal Kyiv City), mykhailoisupov kyiv, endrusmah, MaksimPrykhodko.
at_risk_masking: Only mykhailoisupov/kyiv-air-alert-forecast masks properly: origins are only quiet hours (940 test origins). It explains why: 57% of hours with an alert in the next hour already had one active. mykhailoisupov national does not mask during training, but reports a 'no alert at forecast time' subset (88% of forecasts). yeliena-bochagova does not need a mask (daily start target; ongoing alerts do not make the label positive). MaksimPrykhodko has no mask, and its lags are on the start series, so hours inside an alert stay in the data as negatives. The count/minutes repos (Kamenqq, gklymenko, endrusmah) have no at-risk concept.
data_sources: Vadimkin/ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset in every repo except mykhailoisupov/kyiv. Volunteer file (eTryvoga) as the target: Kamenqq (snapshot 2025-09-01 -> 2026-10-11, plus Telegram air_alert_ua and tryvoga_chomu), mykhailoisupov national (2025-01-01 -> 2026-10-11, plus 26,338 @kpszsu Telegram posts from 2026-04-01), yeliena-bochagova (2022-02-25 -> 2026-10-10), endrusmah (200 commit-pinned daily snapshots 2026-03-24 -> 2026-10-09, plus GDELT GKG headlines), MaksimPrykhodko (2022-02-25 -> 2026-06-24). Official file only: gklymenko (2022-03-15 -> 2026-06-21, oblast-level subset; volunteer used only as a cross-check). mykhailoisupov kyiv: Kyiv Digital open API (Kyiv City, Feb 2022 -> 2026-10-12, minute resolution, no key), checked against the city's weekly open-data file (all 2,641 alerts match), plus @kpszsu posts for a text ablation.
data_source_variant: Most of the cohort moved to the VOLUNTEER file, because the official file froze on 2026-09-07 and they wanted a test window that ran to October. That breaks two of our rules: volunteer data only covers oblast level, and about 5% of its end times are imputed 'naive' +30 min. Kamenqq first mixed the sources and got -16% skill and a -0.57 bias, because the target's meaning changed when the official file stopped. It then switched to eTryvoga alone, a choice made after seeing the test (the author says so). mykhailoisupov national measured volunteer vs official agreement at 82-89% of region-hours. OBLAST-ONLY FILTER PITFALL (gklymenko): it keeps the official file's level=='oblast' rows only. We checked its committed snapshot after removing exact duplicates: oblast-level rows per quarter fall from about 4,500 (2024) to 3,588 (2025Q3), 903 (2025Q4), 138 (2026Q1) and 124 (2026Q2). Every remaining 2026 oblast-level row is Kyiv City. The README's claim that the oblast series 'survives the December-2025 transition intact' holds only for Kyiv City, which has no raions. For every other oblast the filter wipes out the series after late 2025. Kyiv-only repos (mykhailoisupov kyiv, endrusmah, MaksimPrykhodko) give the same reason for picking Kyiv City: it stayed one alert unit through the admin reform.
preprocessing: Deduplication: gklymenko dedupes on (region, started_at, finished_at) and raises an error if duplicates remain (about 50% exact duplicates in the oblast subset); Kamenqq calls drop_duplicates() on both files; yeliena-bochagova only prints the exact-duplicate count and counts starts without deduping; MaksimPrykhodko does not dedupe. Admin union: none of them build a raion/hromada union. Kamenqq maps raion -> oblast only for Telegram posts (data/region_map.csv). Long or standing alerts: gklymenko flags 'always-on' alerts longer than 12 h; mykhailoisupov national cuts all 18 alerts longer than 12 h to start + 30 min (it admits this uses the final length, which is not known live); MaksimPrykhodko drops alerts shorter than 1 min or longer than 7 days; Kamenqq merges intervals into episodes. Gaps: Kamenqq and mykhailoisupov note the 2026-08-30..09-01 official/air_alert_ua outage; mykhailoisupov national drops the last 12 h of the snapshot because running alerts are missing. Time zone: gklymenko keeps the hour-of-day profile in UTC (listed as a limitation); MaksimPrykhodko bins hours in Europe/Kyiv local time, which is fragile around DST changes; mykhailoisupov kyiv converts Kyiv wall-clock API times to UTC and resolves the repeated autumn hour by order.
known_label_artefacts: Naive (+30 min) ends: Kamenqq imputes naive eTryvoga ends with the oblast's median duration, estimated on Sep-Nov 2025 only, before the training window (H6: error 23.9 vs 24.9 min against the +30 default, on 27,846 alerts with a real end). endrusmah and yeliena-bochagova read only started_at, so naive ends cannot leak. mykhailoisupov kyiv avoids the problem with a fully observed city API. Standing / fake long alerts: mykhailoisupov national found that all 18 volunteer alerts longer than 12 h (Jan 2024 - Aug 2026) had almost no matching official alert and treated them as missed all-clears; the cut uses the final length, a stated look-ahead. gklymenko flags them with a 12 h heuristic and excludes always-on frontline oblasts from volume modelling. Gaps: Kamenqq and mykhailoisupov document the 2026-08-30..09-01 outage, but nobody masks it explicitly in evaluation; mykhailoisupov kyiv and endrusmah avoid it by source choice. Duplicates: about 50% exact duplicates in the official oblast subset (gklymenko); in 2022 the Kyiv API stream has 47 repeated starts and 6 repeated all-clears, repaired with an 'all-clear closes the start before it' rule. Source disagreement: Kamenqq reports that since July 2026 eTryvoga records far more Lviv/Volyn alerts than the official data (cause unknown). Live-only fields: mykhailoisupov kyiv uses post-reform alert causes (drone/missile/ballistic) only for alerts that have already ended, because the cause list grows during an alert.
model_family: Kamenqq: HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='poisson'), defaults, retrained for every forecast date; the hourly chances are a 56-day shrunk empirical hour profile scaled by the predicted count. gklymenko: baselines only (Naive, SeasonalNaive, MovingAverage(7)) with empirical-residual intervals. mykhailoisupov kyiv: logistic regression refitted weekly on the previous 16 weeks; challengers are logistic regression on all history and HistGradientBoosting (with and without a CalibratedClassifierCV sigmoid wrapper); a separate conditional-quantile estimator for the remaining alert time. mykhailoisupov national: HistGradientBoostingClassifier per horizon (300 trees, lr 0.05, fixed before the first run), logistic regression on 4 inputs, persistence. yeliena-bochagova: class-balanced logistic regression with a validation-tuned threshold; a constrained random forest was rejected. endrusmah: Poisson GLM with a log link plus a 7-day-level exposure offset (sklearn PoissonRegressor fit on y/exposure with sample_weight=exposure); 36-candidate grid. MaksimPrykhodko: XGBoost tuned with Optuna (n_estimators 116, depth 8, scale_pos_weight 4.9, threshold 0.633), after LR and RF.
features: Lag / own state: counts yesterday, last 7 and 28 days, same weekday last week (Kamenqq); starts in the last 1 h-28 d, minutes under alert in the last 24 h/7 d, time since the last start and all-clear, duration and threat type of the last finished alert, trailing hour-of-day rate (mykhailoisupov kyiv); alert on now, minutes under alert, alert share over 3-168 h, hours since the last alert and the last quiet hour (mykhailoisupov national); rolling start counts and alert-day counts over 3/7/14/30 days, days since the last alert (yeliena-bochagova); city lag 1 and 7, trailing means 3/7/28, collector age (endrusmah); lags 1/2/3/24 h, rolling 3-24 h sums, hours_since_last_alert (MaksimPrykhodko). Spatial: neighbouring oblasts yesterday / 7-day mean from a border table (Kamenqq, H4: small validation gain, no gain on test); current state of all 24 regions and national share now, 1 h ago and over 6 h (mykhailoisupov national; dropping the other regions cost 0.006 skill at 1 h); national context on day D (yeliena-bochagova; rejected); neighbour aggregate lag 1 and mean 7 (endrusmah); 5 Kyiv neighbours at 1-3 h lags (MaksimPrykhodko). Calendar: Kyiv hour and weekday (most repos); sin/cos encodings (endrusmah, MaksimPrykhodko); month (yeliena-bochagova). External: Telegram keyword counts from tryvoga_chomu (Kamenqq) and @kpszsu (both mykhailoisupov repos); GDELT GKG headline count, tone, conflict-theme share and up to 50 TF-IDF unigrams (endrusmah).
external_feature_timing: Better than in pre-2026 repos. mykhailoisupov (both repos): posts strictly before t, from the public t.me/s preview; edited posts keep their timestamp but their text is ignored. Text added +4.0% Brier skill at 1 h on Kyiv (CI +0.4 to +7.3) and nothing at 3/6 h. In the national repo it added 0.025 on validation but only 0.004 on test (CI -0.004 to 0.013), and the gain faded within a week because the channel drifted from 101 to 255 posts/day and named known regions less often (88% -> 79%). Kamenqq: Telegram posts published before 00:00 Kyiv of D; the live repo's ~05:00 UTC daily update delay is not simulated (stated). endrusmah has the strictest timing: an alert snapshot can be used only once the upstream GitHub publisher workflow has completed + 6 h, before the origin; GDELT records need an explicit publication timestamp plus a 2 h buffer for index/archive availability (1,349 records without it were excluded). Its news model did not help: MAE difference +0.046, 7-day block bootstrap CI [-0.059, +0.106]. All Telegram backfills are after-the-fact: deleted posts are missing and only final text is visible.
ablation_design: Mostly fair: additions are compared on the same folds and windows. mykhailoisupov kyiv runs text with/without on the same weekly folds at hourly and 15-minute origins, a training-window sensitivity (8/16/32 weeks/all history), and trees with/without the calibration wrapper. That last comparison exposed a false claim ('trees failed outright'): with the wrapper, Brier 0.270 and AUC 0.51; without it, 0.250 and AUC 0.63. mykhailoisupov national ablates on validation only: other regions on/off, training history from 2023 / 2025 / May 2026, richer text features (0.3133 vs 0.3130 -> dropped). Kamenqq decided H4 neighbours on the validation window (2.028 -> 2.010 MAE), then saw a tie on test. endrusmah compares history-only vs news Poisson on the same origins with a paired block bootstrap. MaksimPrykhodko's 'ablation' (LR -> LR+features -> RF -> XGB) is not interpretable: thresholds were tuned on the test set and the hours_since_last_alert leak enters at the LR+features step.
split_scheme: Kamenqq: validation 2026-08-16..09-12, test 2026-09-13..10-10 (28 days, 4,704 forecasts); Poisson retrained for every forecast date. gklymenko: expanding-window walk-forward, h=1 day, 2022-03-15..2026-06-21, no fixed test. mykhailoisupov kyiv: test = latest 8 weeks, 17 Aug - 12 Oct 2026, weekly folds; each fold trains on origins whose label window closed before the fold starts. mykhailoisupov national: fit 2025-01-01 -> validation 2026-08-16..09-13 -> test 2026-09-13..10-11, model fitted once and frozen 4 weeks; training rows kept only if their label was known before the window's first forecast. yeliena-bochagova: latest 30 days = evaluation, the 30 days before = validation, with a one-forecast-day purge gap; plus a 6-fold rolling backtest (30 d validation / 30 d evaluation, 90-day steps). endrusmah: validation targets 13 Aug - 9 Sep, selection instant 10 Sep 12:00 UTC (10 Sep target purged), test targets 11 Sep - 8 Oct with daily as-of refits under locked settings. MaksimPrykhodko: chronological 80/20 split by ROW INDEX (iloc), no purge, Optuna with TimeSeriesSplit(3) on train.
metrics: Count/continuous: MAE, RMSE, bias, skill vs 7-day average (Kamenqq); MAE, RMSE, MASE, 80% PI coverage, interval width, pinball loss (gklymenko); MAE/RMSE, interval coverage (endrusmah). Probabilistic: Brier, Brier skill, reliability (Kamenqq hourly chances; mykhailoisupov kyiv); Brier skill vs climatology, log loss, PR-AUC, ROC-AUC pooled and within-region (mykhailoisupov national). MISUSED ACCURACY METRICS: yeliena-bochagova's primary metric is balanced accuracy at a threshold, with recall, precision, F1 and FP/FN. That throws away the probabilities, and with an 87.2% positive rate in the last 30 days (Zakarpatska 0%, Ivano-Frankivska 27%, most oblasts ~97-100%) much of the score is just telling regions apart. MaksimPrykhodko headlines F1 0.87, precision 100%, recall 77% and accuracy 98% at a 6-8% base rate, with the F1-optimal threshold picked on the test set; its only baseline is 'always predict 0'.
unit_of_metric: Pooled in most repos. mykhailoisupov national reports both: pooled AUC 0.86 vs within-region 0.76 at 1 h, and says outright that pooled AUC mostly reflects knowing which regions are busy. Single-unit repos (Kyiv City) avoid the question. yeliena-bochagova shows per-region balanced accuracy only as a diagnostic, and warns that some regions have one class in 30 days.
baseline_strength: Strong baselines in mykhailoisupov kyiv: flat 28-day rate, hour-of-day rate over 28 days (the pre-registered reference), hour-of-day rate over all history, and a recent-onset rate (28-day rate conditional on a start in the previous H). The author found the pre-registered reference was weaker than a flat rate, so skill vs that reference overstated the model. Headlines then moved to the 'best simple forecast chosen after the fact on the same period', which deliberately raises the bar. Kamenqq: last-7-days average (ties the model: 1.97 vs 1.97 MAE) and same weekday last week; for hourly chances, a flat rate (wins on Brier: 0.1870 vs 0.1871 at 1 day). gklymenko: Naive, SeasonalNaive, MA(7); MASE ~1, SeasonalNaive worst. mykhailoisupov national: 28-day hour-of-day climatology and calibrated persistence (per-region alert rate given state now, last 90 days); no rolling recent-rate baseline. endrusmah: the 28-day mean benchmark beats every Poisson (final MAE 1.297 vs 1.518 for the deployed choice). Rolling means were kept OUT of the selection pool by design, so the deployed model is knowingly worse. yeliena-bochagova: always-alert and persistence only. MaksimPrykhodko: always 0 only.
calibration: Kamenqq: reliability check at 1 day ahead (35% -> 35%, 45% -> 46%, 74% -> 76%; low chances run too low, 3% -> 6%, and 25% -> 38% for 2-hour windows). mykhailoisupov kyiv: reliability plot; calibration 'rough' bin by bin; the highest 1 h forecasts are too high. Its sigmoid CalibratedClassifierCV (3 folds) wrecked the trees: mean forecast 12% vs 33% observed. mykhailoisupov national: within 0.04 in every 10-point band at 1 h. endrusmah: empirical residual intervals cover all 28 outcomes, but they are 9.11 starts/day wide. gklymenko: 80% PI covers only ~72% (heavy tails); lower bound goes negative. yeliena-bochagova and MaksimPrykhodko: no calibration; class_weight='balanced' / scale_pos_weight distort the probabilities by construction.
calibration_under_drift: mykhailoisupov kyiv checks calibration-in-the-large under the regime change: after the 7 Sep reform, the all-history logistic averages a 74% 6 h forecast against 87% observed; the 16-week model averages 82%. Kyiv starts per day went from 1.2-1.9 to 5.5 since August 2026, and the median quiet gap fell from 5-11 h to 1.4 h. endrusmah: the label mean rose from 1.85 in the initial training portion to 3.75 in validation; the fix was a 7-day-level exposure offset (multiplicative adjustment to the known recent level). Kamenqq: count bias -0.09/day on test; per-oblast skill ranges from +11% (Chernivetska) to -32% (Kyiv City). The national mykhailoisupov repo shows the Telegram gain fading over the 4 frozen weeks (0.018, 0.002, 0.002, -0.003). No repo fits a recalibration on a later window.
uncertainty_of_gain: mykhailoisupov kyiv: 1,000-draw day-block bootstrap on Brier skill. vs best simple forecast: +3.2% (-2.5 to +8.5) at 1 h, +3.3% (-4.7 to +11.1) at 3 h, +5.1% (-4.6 to +13.6) at 6 h, all CIs include zero; since the reform +10.2% (+0.2 to +22.9) at 3 h and +11.8% (+1.2 to +19.9) at 6 h. mykhailoisupov national: 2,000-draw day-block bootstrap; Telegram gain CI -0.004 to 0.013 on test. endrusmah: paired 7-day moving-block bootstrap on the MAE difference [-0.059, +0.106]. Kamenqq, gklymenko, yeliena-bochagova and MaksimPrykhodko report no CI on gains.
regime_coverage: Several repos test inside the Sep-2026 yellow/red regime because they use volunteer data or the Kyiv API up to October: Kamenqq (13 Sep-10 Oct), mykhailoisupov national (13 Sep-11 Oct), endrusmah (11 Sep-8 Oct), yeliena-bochagova (last 30 days to 10 Oct), and mykhailoisupov kyiv (17 Aug-12 Oct, with a separate 'since 7 Sep reform' slice; only 25 red-level alerts). The Aug-2026 surge (Kyiv 5.5 starts/day) falls inside most test windows. gklymenko marks the Dec-2025 aggregation change but does not see that it breaks every oblast series except Kyiv City. MaksimPrykhodko's test is the last 20% of rows ending 2026-06-24, before the reform. None evaluates a pre-reform frozen model on post-reform data the way our D-015 does; the closest is mykhailoisupov kyiv's 'since reform' slice.
leakage_handling: Strong examples. mykhailoisupov kyiv: a hide-the-future recompute test on synthetic and real data, a NEGATIVE CONTROL (a planted leaky feature must be caught, and exactly that one), fold labels must close before each test fold, every still-open label is flipped and baselines must not change, truncate() blanks running alerts' end and final cause list, and the live forecast equals the backtest for the same instant. mykhailoisupov national: future values flipped at 3 cut points; 9 planted leaks all caught. Kamenqq: full-data vs truncated-data recompute must be identical; deliberate breaks each fail a test; two review agents rebuilt 8 real forecast days from cut data. endrusmah: 25 temporal/provenance tests (future label/text injection, final-truth isolation, test-era corruption, lock integrity), selection stage physically cannot construct test rows, SHA-256 lock on the selection. yeliena-bochagova: one-day purge gap and invariant tests. Missed / leaky: mykhailoisupov national cuts fake long alerts using their final length (stated look-ahead). MaksimPrykhodko has a direct TARGET LEAK in hours_since_last_alert: on label=1 rows the feature is set to the gap to the previous alert, and on label=0 rows it is the previous row's value + 1. So the feature drops exactly in the hours whose own label is 1. We re-implemented it on Kamenqq's committed volunteer snapshot (Kyiv City, the same 80/20 row split, a HistGradientBoosting classifier, F1-optimal threshold on test). With the leaky feature: F1 0.82, precision 0.98, recall 0.71. With a causal version (shifted ffill of the last alert position): F1 0.14, precision 0.08, recall 0.48 (base rate 8.3%). That matches the repo's '100% precision, 0.87 F1' and its 'most important feature (SHAP 0.66)'. It also tunes the threshold on the test set and splits by row index without a purge.
test_window_hygiene: Mixed, and most authors say so honestly. Kamenqq: H4 and the 'when' method were chosen on validation and test was scored once, but the target-source switch (official+Telegram -> eTryvoga only) came after seeing test results; the extra 'details' checks were measured once with nothing changed. mykhailoisupov kyiv: the window, inputs and reference were fixed in advance, but the final model (16-week window) replaced the first attempt AFTER test results were seen, and the headline bar ('best simple forecast') is chosen ex post. The README and REFLECTION.txt document both. mykhailoisupov national: choices committed on validation, test run once (git history: 'Fix the model choice on validation' at 18:31, 'Score the test window once' at 18:35). endrusmah: v1 had already scored 11 Sep - 8 Oct; v0.2 locked selection with a SHA-256 hash and passed 25 tests before re-scoring, and calls it a 'reused historical holdout'. yeliena-bochagova: 'the latest period was inspected during development', so it points to the rolling backtest as the stronger evidence. MaksimPrykhodko: threshold tuned on test; no hygiene.
headline_results: Kamenqq: count MAE 1.97 vs 1.97 for the 7-day average (tie, skill ~0%); hourly chance Brier 0.1871 vs flat 0.1870 at 1 day (does not beat the flat rate), well calibrated. gklymenko: Kyiv City minutes/day MAE MA(7) 96.3 vs Naive 110.2 vs SeasonalNaive 116.6; MASE 1.03-1.25 (no baseline beats seasonal naive meaningfully); PI coverage 72% vs nominal 80%. mykhailoisupov kyiv (onset, quiet hours): Brier 0.218 / 0.217 / 0.157 at 1/3/6 h vs best simple 0.225 / 0.225 / 0.165, edges +3.2% / +3.3% / +5.1% with CIs including zero; since reform +10-12% at 3-6 h (CIs exclude zero); base rates 33% / 60% / 75%; ROC-AUC 0.63 at 1 h. mykhailoisupov national (state): BSS vs climatology 0.267 at 1 h, but 0.065 on quiet rows and 0.007 at 24 h; within-region AUC 0.76 (all) / 0.62 (quiet). yeliena-bochagova: balanced accuracy 0.932 latest vs persistence 0.865; rolling backtest 0.855 vs 0.764, with more false negatives than persistence (594 vs 386). endrusmah: the deployed Poisson loses to the 28-day mean (final MAE 1.518 vs 1.297). MaksimPrykhodko: F1 0.87 / precision 1.00 / accuracy 0.98, an artefact of the target leak (see leakage_handling). Across the cohort, wherever a strong rolling baseline exists, the model ties it or beats it by a small margin that is not significant.
code_available: All public on GitHub. Licenses: endrusmah MIT (+ upstream license preserved); MaksimPrykhodko MIT; the others have no license. Data committed in the repo: Kamenqq (frozen data/snapshot/ with volunteer, official and Telegram CSVs, ~24 MB), gklymenko (data/raw/ CSVs), yeliena-bochagova (processed panel), endrusmah (compact commit-pinned snapshot extracts + GDELT JSON with SHA-256). mykhailoisupov downloads at run time (uv.lock / pinned). CI: Kamenqq (GitHub Actions on 3 OS x Python 3.9-3.15, 98 tests). Test counts: Kamenqq 98, gklymenko 62, mykhailoisupov national 47, endrusmah 25. Maintenance: all are deadline snapshots (Oct 2026, or June 2026 for gklymenko and MaksimPrykhodko); no ongoing maintenance expected.
takeaways_for_project: 1) Target: our onset + at-risk mask (CLAUDE.md Target section) is supported by two cohort measurements. One model's state-target skill falls from 0.267 to 0.065 on quiet rows (mykhailoisupov national), and 57% of hours with an alert in the next hour already had one active (mykhailoisupov kyiv). Cite both in the README as external motivation for the mask. 2) Oblast-only filter: gklymenko's level=='oblast' series is empty for every oblast except Kyiv City after 2025Q4 (138 rows/quarter, all Kyiv City). This validates our union of all levels via the `oblast` column, and suggests a data-quality check that raises if any unit's onsets per month collapse by more than ~90% across Dec 2025 (D-017 item 6). 3) Volunteer data: the cohort's move to volunteer data to reach October is the trap our 'never use volunteer_data' rule and D-007/D-015 avoid. Kamenqq showed that mixing sources across a source stop gives -16% skill and -0.57 bias; that is evidence for 'never mix the two sources in one training set or one test metric'. 4) Baselines: every repo with a rolling recent baseline (7/28-day mean, flat 28-day rate, recent-onset rate) found the model ties it or beats it within noise. Expect the same against our rolling recent-rate baseline (D-021), and treat a tie as a valid result. mykhailoisupov's finding that a pre-registered hour-of-day reference was weaker than a flat rate suggests adding a flat recent rate as a sanity row, so skill vs climatology is not overstated. 5) Metrics: avoid balanced accuracy / F1 / precision at a threshold as headlines (yeliena-bochagova, MaksimPrykhodko); keep Brier/BSS primary and report within-oblast AUC next to pooled AUC (mykhailoisupov national: 0.86 pooled vs 0.76 within). 6) Leakage: MaksimPrykhodko's hours_since_last_alert bug is a ready template for our negative control in tests/test_leakage.py: a 'time since last onset' feature that resets on the current row's label must be caught by the truncation test. Our minutes_since_last_start must use only onsets at or before t. 7) Calibration: do not wrap GBMs in CalibratedClassifierCV on the training folds. mykhailoisupov saw it collapse the mean forecast from 27% to 12%. Our D-021 rule (calibration fitted on validation, applied to the same model) is the safer design. 8) Drift: mean predicted vs observed after the reform (74% vs 87% for an all-history model) is exactly the calibration-in-the-large check in our D-015(c); expect a frozen pre-reform model to under-forecast onsets after Aug-Sep 2026. 9) Uncertainty: day- or week-block bootstrap on skill (mykhailoisupov, endrusmah) is the norm in the better repos; adopt the D-013 week-block CI if time allows.
best_practices: ADOPT: (a) a negative-control leaky feature that the truncation test must catch, plus planted-leak counts (mykhailoisupov: 9 planted leaks all caught); (b) flipping every not-yet-closed label and asserting baselines do not change (a direct test of D-021 label maturity); (c) live forecast == backtest forecast for the same instant (useful for M5/M6); (d) a locked selection artefact with a SHA-256 hash checked before the final scoring (endrusmah), which fits our 'final test scored ONCE' rule; (e) source provenance with an availability buffer, i.e. data usable only after the publisher workflow has finished + 6 h (endrusmah), relevant to M6 monthly runs; (f) reporting results on all rows next to a quiet-now subset, so the state-target inflation is visible; (g) a REFLECTION / corrections section stating which claims failed (mykhailoisupov's 'boosted trees failed outright' correction); (h) a per-oblast skill table showing the spread (Kamenqq: +11% to -32%). AVOID: (1) filtering the official file to level=='oblast' (gklymenko); (2) volunteer data as the target, or mixing official and volunteer across a source stop (Kamenqq v1); (3) thresholded accuracy metrics as headlines, class_weight='balanced' on a probability model, and thresholds tuned on test (yeliena-bochagova, MaksimPrykhodko); (4) splitting by row index (iloc 80/20) with no purge (MaksimPrykhodko); (5) features computed with the current row's label (hours_since_last_alert); (6) cutting long alerts using their final duration (mykhailoisupov national), which our causal 24 h rule (D-020) avoids; (7) choosing the headline baseline or the model window after seeing test results, even when disclosed (mykhailoisupov kyiv, Kamenqq); (8) keeping strong baselines out of the selection pool and then deploying a model that loses to them (endrusmah); (9) hour-of-day profiles in UTC (gklymenko) or hourly bins in Kyiv local time across DST changes (MaksimPrykhodko); our rule (UTC grid, Kyiv only for calendar features) is right.
